title: traffic-twin behaviour rules (tt.rules/v1)
description: Entities (with relations, ownership-aware reads and list shapes) plus cause/effect and batch rules (revision 1.6: pre-existing entities per customer, keyed state without an id, removal effects, reads selected by request body members). Delays are figurative (decision D1): a single duration or a {min, max} range drawn with the seed. Cross-field checks (outcome probabilities sum to 1, referenced effects exist and belong to the same outcome, no cycles in after_effect, ${effect:...} references only to earlier effects of the same chain, relation targets exist) are enforced by tt-core and by pack readers, not by this schema.

ttPath.description: tt-path of sanitizer.md 5.0; .@name and .#text (v1.19) reach the attributes and the mixed text of XML bodies.

seed.description: Rules v1.6: objects that exist before any session, per customer (an entity no write creates, read by its owner). The world generator gives every synthetic customer a number of them drawn from per_customer.

per_customer.description: Buckets of objects per customer and their shares (sum 1, checked by tt-core); every bucket was seen for at least k_min subjects.

values.description: Shares of the clear values of some fields of the objects (each value seen for at least k_min owners): field path -> value -> share (sum 1).

subjects.description: Exact number of subjects the distribution counts.

key.description: Rules v1.6: the records have no id of their own; a record is identified by its owner (the session customer) and/or the values of fields. Excludes created_by.

upserted_by.description: Rules v1.6, with key: writes that create or replace the record whose key they carry.

service.description: Service that exposes the operation; default: the entity's service.

by.description: Absent: every entity owned by the session's customer (lists), or the record of a keyed entity selected by key.

hidden_when.description: Entities whose fields equal all these literal values are not exposed by this operation.

scope.description: owner: only entities owned by the session's customer (or without owner) are exposed.

foreign.description: With scope owner: answer when the selection designates another customer's entity or owner.

foreign_example.description: Named contract example used for the foreign answer (default: the first example of that status).

not_found_example.description: Named contract example used when a single-object read finds nothing (default: the first 404 example).

key.description: Rules v1.6, keyed entities: the request parameters holding the values of the key fields.

removed_status.description: Rules v1.6: status of a single-object read of an entity removed in the session (default: as an entity that does not exist).

relations.description: Fields of this entity that hold the id of another entity (foreign keys).

many.description: true: the field holds an array of ids.

origin.description: Who wrote the rule (v1.4): mined (default when absent) or manual (rule editor).

match.description: Rules v1.9: conditions on the request and on the customer; all must hold or the rule does not fire.

target_id.description: Update the existing entity whose id is this bound variable (alternative to target).

target_key.description: Rules v1.8: the record of a keyed entity (key/upserted_by): every key field with a bound ${var} or a literal; {} is the customer's singleton. With set the record is created when missing; with remove it is deleted.

set.description: Values: literals, ${var}, ${effect:id}; since v1.7 also ${not:field}, the opposite of the target's boolean field (a toggle); since v1.10 derived values.

respond.description: Response effect (v1.4): from the instant it applies, the session's calls to service/op answer status (the named contract example, else the first of that status; body, when present, wins) with probability p each (default 1), for at most times calls (0 or absent: no limit). Used for 'the next call returns Y' (times 1) and 'errors with frequency p'.

body.description: Example error body typed by a person (rules 1.10): wins over example; at most 16 KiB; the gate runs the personal data detectors on it.

limit.description: Rules v1.8: a counter per key. Every application of the effect counts one call for its key; a call of service/op answers status when at least n counted calls with the same key fall within window before it (absent: the whole session). key is a ${var} bound to the request of the cause (then service/op are the cause's); absent: per customer. Excludes times.

until.description: Rules v1.9: a precondition. From the start of the session the calls answer status until the effect applies (the cause was seen); excludes times, limit and p.

remove.description: Rules v1.6: the target entity (target or target_id) is removed: it leaves the lists and its single-object reads answer as removed (read_by.removed_status, else not found).

where.description: Rules v1.7: a guard of a target or target_id set: the effect applies only while the entity's fields equal these literal values (a later spontaneous step of a lifecycle does not undo the state a write set).

target_all.description: Rules v1.9: every entity of entity owned by the customer of the cause that matches where gets set (or is removed). Cannot be the target or ${effect:} of another effect.

when.description: Rules v1.9: the outcome is eligible only when all conditions hold. Eligible outcomes are those whose when holds; when none does, the outcomes without when. The draw is weighted by p among the eligible ones; p are joint probabilities and sum to 1 over all outcomes.

keys.description: Correlation keys found by the miner: two event locations that carry the same token (same HMAC domain).

matches.description: Exact count of causes whose token was found at both ends.

origin.description: Who wrote the rule (v1.4): mined (default when absent) or manual (rule editor).

fieldPath.description: Dotted path into the entity: a.b is field b inside object a.

delay.description: Figurative delay: one duration, or a range {min, max} (min <= max) from which the world generator and the mock draw a uniform whole number of seconds with the seed.

bindRef.description: A variable bound by cause.bind, written ${name}.

nameRef.description: A named request parameter (used by list pagination).

selector.description: How a read selects entities: a ref (by id, or by a top-level field with `field`), or a request parameter compared with the owner customer id (`owner: true`). Since v1.6 a request body member outside arrays selects too ($.filters.customerId, $.variables.id), by id, field or owner.

listShape.description: Envelope and pagination of a list read (at path ends with [*]).

count.description: Where the number of items of this page goes in resp.body.

total.description: Where the number of matching items (all pages) goes in resp.body.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor parameter; values are minted by the mock (rules.md section 2.4).

next_cursor.description: Where the cursor of the next page goes in resp.body; requires cursor.

filters.description: Rules v1.9: keep the items whose field equals the value of the request parameter, when the request carries it.

derivedValue.description: Derived value (rules 1.10, docs/spec/rules.md 3.15): computed when the effect applies. Arguments are numbers, references (${var}, ${field:path} with [*] for every item, ${effect:id}, ${now}) or nested derived values (at most 4 levels); a text argument only for copy. Cross-field checks (variables bound, effects earlier ancestors, argument counts, offsets, templates) are done by tt-core and the pack loader.

effectValues.description: Values of create and set (rules 1.10): scalars, references or derived values.

keyRefs.description: Key field -> where the request carries its value (a request parameter or a request body member outside arrays).

match.description: Rules v1.9: one condition. A request value (at: req.body path outside arrays, req.query/req.headers/req.path name) or a customer attribute (customer) is one of in (canonical scalar comparison: a number, also a string that is one, by value) or a number in [min, max). A missing value never matches.

attribute.description: Rules v1.9: a customer attribute carried by responses (one value per customer). The world gives each synthetic customer a value drawn from values; the mock keeps one value per session and writes it at every field.

aggregate.description: Rules v1.9: a number of a response computed at read time: count of the customer's entities matching where, sum of a numeric field, or the base value moved by by at every successful call of the delta operations.

listOp.description: Rules v1.9: a list operation that no entity reads; the mock pages its static answer (a page beyond the first is empty).
